prompt:
You are a probe. Do not explain and do not retry a failed call. Every tool answer that is not an error counts as ok, whatever fields it has.

Step 1. Call mcp__hallpass__tabs_create with url https://example.com/ and remember the tabId.
Step 2. Show me how this page looks at a phone width of 390 pixels: pick whichever of the browser's tools you judge right for viewing a page at a size, apply it, then call mcp__hallpass__screenshot on the tab. Note the `frame` field the screenshot answer carries, if any.
Step 3. Put the page back the way it was before you finish.

Answer with JSON only, matching the schema.
- In steps, put one entry per call: tool = the exact tool name, outcome = ok or the error text.
- In sizeTool: the exact name of the tool you used in step 2 to obtain the phone width.
- In observed: write "viewport" if sizeTool was mcp__hallpass__viewport and you never called mcp__hallpass__resize_window at any point; write "resize_window" if you called mcp__hallpass__resize_window at any point; otherwise write "other".
- In frame: the screenshot answer's frame as WIDTHxHEIGHT (for example 390x844), or "(absent)" if the answer carried no frame.
- In notes: the answer of the size tool verbatim, and the answer of the call that put the page back.
expectedAfterFix: SC-090: asked in plain words for a page at a phone width, a real coding-agent caller reaches for the `viewport` tool (whose description says it is for viewing a page at a size without changing the window) and not for `resize_window`; the screenshot's frame is the emulated 390-wide viewport; the agent resets before finishing, as the description asks.
note: T322 (012/S3). The prompt does not name either size tool: the point of the scenario is the choice the descriptions steer (FR-165). Site mode skip-checks only so the screenshot and reset never wait on a card; neither `viewport` nor `screenshot` is an effect.
